lectures.title: Political parties: timeline, the Congress System and national party status

parts.t: Historical timeline of political parties and splits
items: First President: Atal Bihari Vajpayee; successor to BJS
Split from INC by Sharad Pawar, P.A. Sangma, Tariq Anwar

**"One-Party Dominant System" / "Congress System":** term coined by political scientist **Rajni Kothari** to characterize India's democratic, multi-party electoral landscape dominated by the Congress party post-independence.
**End of the "Congress System":** marked by the **1989 General Election**, ushering in the era of minority/coalition governments.
**1989:** V.P. Singh led the National Front with outside support from BJP + Left.
**National Party Threshold:** requires ≥ 6% votes in 4 States + 4 Lok Sabha seats.
Both conditions (≥ 6% votes in 4 States and 4 Lok Sabha seats) are mandatory under **Route 2**.
**Constitutional Body:** an authority or institution directly established, empowered, and anchored within the text of the Constitution of India.
**Statutory Bodies:** bodies set up by Law/Act.
**Extra-Constitutional / Non-Statutory Body:** established via an Executive Order or Cabinet Resolution (Executive Resolution), e.g., NITI Aayog, Planning Commission, NDC.
The **Planning Commission (1950)** and **NITI Aayog (2015)** are Extra-Constitutional Bodies (NOT Constitutional, NOT Statutory).

**Local Body Elections:** conducted solely by the State Election Commission (Art. 243-K), NOT by the Election Commission of India.
**Local Body Financial Devolution:** recommended by the State Finance Commission (Art. 243-I) to the Governor.

**Article 148(3) & 148(6):** salary, pension, and administrative expenses of CAG charged on the CFI.
**"Who is NOT Charged on CFI?" Elimination Trio - Election Commission of India:** salaries and administrative expenses are votable (NOT listed under Article 112(3) charged items).
**First Experimental Use:** 19 May 1982 in the Parur Assembly Constituency, Kerala (A.C. Jose v. Sivan Pillai case).
**Statutory backing:** introduced experimentally; later backed by statutory amendments to the RPA, 1951 (Section 61A in 1989).

**Constitutional Machinery (Art. 324):** EVMs are deployed under the superintendence, direction, and control of the Election Commission of India (ECI) for Lok Sabha and State Legislative Assembly elections.
**Voting Device vs. Electoral System:** EVM is an electronic vote recording and counting apparatus, NOT an electoral system.
**First-Past-the-Post (FPTP):** India conducts direct general elections using the FPTP system, where the candidate with the highest valid votes wins, irrespective of crossing 50%.
**First State Fully Covered by EVMs:** Goa was the first State to conduct an entire General Assembly election using EVMs across all constituencies (June 1999).
**First General Election Entirely on EVMs:** the 14th Lok Sabha General Election (2004) was the first nationwide general election conducted entirely using EVMs.

parts.t: Major electoral technology and reform milestones
items: First experimental use: Parur Assembly Constituency, Kerala
Introduced experimentally; Section 61A of the RPA, 1951 in 1989.
Nationwide rollout initiated under CEC T.N. Seshan
Established voter photo-identification to prevent bogus voting and impersonation.
First used experimentally in the Noksen Assembly by-election, Nagaland
Generates an independent paper slip verification visible to the voter for 7 seconds.
PUCL v. Union of India (2013); added negative voting choice button on ballot units.
**The 2013 Sequencing Trap:** VVPAT was introduced first (4 September 2013); NOTA was mandated later in the same month (27 September 2013).

**Definition & Objective:** NOTA (None of the Above) is an electoral option provided on ballot papers and Electronic Voting Machines (EVMs) enabling voters to exercise a negative vote and formally reject all contesting candidates in secret.

**Judicial Origin:** directed by the Supreme Court of India in the landmark judgment PUCL v. Union of India on 27 September 2013; the Supreme Court directs mandatory introduction of the NOTA button on EVMs.
**Constitutional Foundation:** the Supreme Court linked the right to register a negative vote in secrecy with the Freedom of Speech and Expression under Article 19(1)(a).
**Abstention vs. Active Participation:** exercising NOTA is NOT non-voting/abstaining; it is the active exercise of the statutory right to vote by registering a neutral/negative choice.
**Rajya Sabha Elections:** NOTA is NOT applicable in Rajya Sabha and Legislative Council elections (struck down by SC in 2018; limited to direct Lok Sabha & Assembly elections).

parts.t: NOTA, old Rule 49-O and the Right to Reject
items: Voter attends polling booth and presses the NOTA button on EVM
Symbolic Expression ONLY; candidate with highest valid votes among contestants is declared elected
Voter entered booth and refused to vote before Presiding Officer
Violated (Recorded in Form 17-A; struck down as ultra vires)
Re-election mandated if rejection crosses a threshold (>50%) (NOT applicable in India)
**Automatic Invalidation Fallacy:** the statement "If NOTA receives the majority/highest votes, the election is cancelled and a fresh poll is held" is FALSE.

**Legal Position:** under the First-Past-the-Post system, even if NOTA receives the maximum votes, the contesting candidate securing the highest number of valid votes among the candidates is declared elected.

lectures.title: Comptroller and Auditor General of India (CAG)

items: **Constitutional Framework:** governed under Part V, Chapter V (Articles 148–151).
**Constitutional Identity:** an independent constitutional authority designated as the Guardian of the Public Purse / Public Finance and the head of the Indian Audit and Accounts Department.
**Constitutional Weight:** described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the most important officer under the Constitution of India.
**Four bulwarks of the democratic system:** the CAG is one of the four, along with SC, UPSC, and ECI.
**Statutory Milestone (1971):** CAG's (Duties, Powers and Conditions of Service) Act, 1971.
Comptroller and Auditor General of India
Appointment, oath, tenure, removal, post-retirement ban, salary & charged expenses.
Duties and Powers of the CAG
Auditing authority over receipts, expenditures, stores, and accounts of Union & States.
Form of Accounts of the Union and of the States
Prescribed by the President on the advice of the CAG (Trap: CAG advises, President prescribes).
Submitted to the President, who causes them to be laid before both Houses of Parliament.
Submitted to the Governor, who causes them to be laid before the State Legislature.
**Form of Accounts Advice Trap (Art. 150):** accounts are kept in the form prescribed by the President, upon the advice of the CAG (NOT by the CAG unilaterally).
Appointed by warrant under hand and seal (Trap: NOT PM, Finance Minister, or PAC).
6 Years OR 65 Years of Age (Whichever is earlier)
Dual cap rule (Trap: NOT 5 years / 62 years).
President of India following Parliamentary process
Removed on the same grounds & manner as a Supreme Court Judge.
Ineligible for any further office under the Government of India OR Government of any State.
Indian Polity #80; Indian Polity #65; Indian Polity #78
**Removal:** by an Address by both Houses via Special Majority on proved misbehaviour/incapacity.

**Post-Retirement Ban:** CAG cannot take up any further office under either the Central or State Governments (like the UPSC Chairman, who cannot take another job; unlike judges, who can head commissions).
Cannot be varied to disadvantage after appointment.
Charged on Consolidated Fund of India
All salaries, allowances, and pensions of CAG and staff are Charged (Non-votable).
Audits all expenditure from CFI, Consolidated Fund of States & UTs with Assemblies.
Audits all transactions relating to Contingency Funds and Public Accounts of Union and States.
Audits manufacturing, trading, profit/loss accounts, stores/stocks, and PSUs.
Evaluates Economy, Efficiency, and Effectiveness of government schemes and outlays.

parts.t: What the CAG does not do
items: Does not control the issue/drawal of money from the treasury, unlike the British CAG.
Relieved of Union account compilation since 1976 (handled by CGA under Ministry of Finance).
Has no power to disallow expenditure, enforce recovery, or initiate criminal prosecutions.
**Universal Golden Trap:** in India, CAG is an Auditor General, NOT a Comptroller.
**Comptroller vs. Auditor Trap:** the statement "CAG ensures no money is drawn from the Consolidated Fund of India without prior sanction" is FALSE (audit is post-expenditure / ex-post facto).
**1976 Separation Reform:** departmentalization of Union accounts separated Accounting from Auditing.
**1 March 1976:** CAG was relieved of the responsibility of preparing Union accounts with effect from this date; continues to compile and maintain accounts of most States.
**Initial Report Routing Trap:** the CAG does NOT submit reports directly to the PAC or Parliament; reports are submitted strictly to the President/Governor first.
**Report Submission Destination Trap:** the statement "CAG submits audit reports directly to the Public Accounts Committee" is FALSE (submitted to President/Governor under Art. 151).
**Relationship with PAC:** CAG acts as the "Friend, Philosopher, and Guide" of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC), attending meetings and assisting in the line-by-line examination of audit reports.
**Ultimate Enforcing Authority:** the ultimate constitutional responsibility for taking action on the findings in CAG reports rests with Parliament / State Legislature.
